PaperTitle: Graph Embedding for Mapping Interdisciplinary Research Networks
Abstract:
Representation learning is the frst step in automating tasks such
as research paper recommendation, classifcation, and retrieval.
Due to the accelerating rate of research publication, together with
the recognised benefts of interdisciplinary research, systems that
facilitate researchers in discovering and understanding relevant
works from beyond their immediate school of knowledge are vital.
This work explores diferent methods of research paper represen-
tation (or document embedding), to identify those methods that
are capable of preserving the interdisciplinary implications of re-
search papers in their embeddings. In addition to evaluating state
of the art methods of document embedding in a interdisciplinary
citation prediction task, we propose a novel Graph Neural Network
architecture designed to preserve the key interdisciplinary impli-
cations of research articles in citation network node embeddings.
Our proposed method outperforms other GNN-based methods in
interdisciplinary citation prediction, without compromising overall
citation prediction performance.
SummaryAbstract: This paper evaluates multiple document-embedding approaches for representing scientific articles with a focus on preserving interdisciplinary relations. It introduces ComBSAGE, a message-passing GNN aggregation method that groups neighbour messages by connected components before aggregation, and shows that ComBSAGE improves interdisciplinary citation prediction while maintaining strong overall citation prediction performance.

References.PaperTitle: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP)
References.SemanticInformation: Introduces SciBERT, a BERT-based pretrained language model trained on a large corpus of scientific text to improve downstream NLP tasks in scientific domains. The authors pretrain the model on a domain-specific corpus and evaluate on scientific NLP benchmarks. They demonstrate that SciBERT yields improved performance over BERT baselines on multiple scientific NLP tasks, indicating benefits of domain-specific pretraining.

References.PaperTitle: A Comprehensive Survey of Graph Embedding: Problems, Techniques, and Applications
References.Publication: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge & Data Engineering
References.SemanticInformation: Presents an extensive survey of graph embedding methods, categorizing problems, techniques, and application areas. It reviews matrix factorization, random walk, deep learning, and neural-network-based methods and discusses evaluation and challenges. The paper synthesizes trends and identifies open issues for future research in graph representation learning.

References.PaperTitle: Measuring and relieving the over-smoothing problem for graph neural networks from the topological view
References.Publication: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
References.SemanticInformation: Investigates the over-smoothing phenomenon in GNNs from a graph-topology perspective, proposing measurements to quantify over-smoothing and methods to alleviate it. The authors analyze when node representations become indistinguishable as depth increases and propose remedies. They empirically validate the measurements and mitigation strategies across datasets to show improved representation quality and task performance.

References.PaperTitle: SPECTER: Document-level Representation Learning using Citation-informed Transformers
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
References.SemanticInformation: Introduces SPECTER, a method that fine-tunes transformer-based text representations using citation relationships to produce document-level embeddings for scientific papers. The model is trained to bring representations of citing and cited papers closer while pushing apart unrelated papers. Evaluations show SPECTER embeddings are effective for tasks like citation prediction and clustering, outperforming purely text-based baselines.

References.PaperTitle: Assessing Network Representations for Identifying Interdisciplinarity
References.Publication: Companion Proceedings of the Web Conference 2022 (WWW '22)
References.SemanticInformation: Examines network representation methods for detecting interdisciplinarity in citation networks. The study compares embedding and network-analysis approaches to identify structural patterns associated with interdisciplinary works. Results highlight which representations capture interdisciplinarity signals and discuss implications for automated identification of interdisciplinary research.

References.PaperTitle: The Structure of Interdisciplinary Science: Uncovering and Explaining Roles in Citation Graphs
References.Publication: Complex Networks and Their Applications XI: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Complex Networks and Their Applications, Vol. 1
References.SemanticInformation: Investigates structural roles that interdisciplinary research occupies in citation graphs and develops methods to uncover and explain those roles. The authors analyze citation network substructures and their relation to interdisciplinarity, using network metrics and role-detection techniques. They provide empirical findings that describe how interdisciplinary works bridge communities and contribute to knowledge transfer across fields.

References.PaperTitle: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (NAACL-HLT 2019)
References.SemanticInformation: Introduces BERT, a transformer-based language model pretrained with masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction to learn deep bidirectional representations. The model can be fine-tuned for a range of NLP tasks with state-of-the-art performance at the time. BERT's architecture and pretraining paradigm significantly improved benchmarks across multiple language understanding tasks.

References.PaperTitle: Graph embedding techniques, applications, and performance: A survey
References.SemanticInformation: Surveys graph-embedding techniques, their applications, and empirical performance evaluations. The paper categorizes methods (matrix factorization, random walk, deep learning) and discusses use-cases like link prediction and node classification. It summarizes challenges and offers guidance on method selection based on application requirements.

References.PaperTitle: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS'17)
References.SemanticInformation: Proposes GraphSAGE, an inductive framework for generating node embeddings by sampling and aggregating features from a node's local neighborhood. GraphSAGE enables embedding of previously unseen nodes and scales to large graphs. Experiments demonstrate that learned aggregators outperform transductive baselines on node-classification and representation tasks.

Introduces variational graph auto-encoders (VGAE), which extend variational autoencoders to graph-structured data for unsupervised learning of node embeddings. The model uses GCNs for encoder and employs probabilistic link reconstruction for training. VGAE is shown to perform well on link prediction and unsupervised representation learning tasks.

References.PaperTitle: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
References.Publication: 5th International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2017), Conference Track Proceedings
References.SemanticInformation: Presents Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for semi-supervised learning on graph-structured data, formulating convolution operations on graphs via spectral methods. The approach integrates node features and graph structure, achieving strong performance on node classification benchmarks. GCNs are efficient and have become a foundational architecture in graph representation learning.

References.PaperTitle: Semantic and relational spaces in science of science: deep learning models for article vectorisation
References.SemanticInformation: Explores deep learning approaches for vectorizing scientific articles, comparing semantic (textual) and relational (citation/network) representation spaces. The authors evaluate models that capture different aspects of articles and discuss their implications for science-of-science analyses. Findings show complementary strengths of semantic and relational embeddings for mapping scholarly landscapes.

A commentary/article in Nature discussing the rise and importance of team-based and interdisciplinary science. It highlights benefits and challenges of collaborative research, emphasizing the trend towards larger, multi-disciplinary teams in addressing complex problems. The piece underscores institutional and cultural factors that shape team science.

References.PaperTitle: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
References.Publication: 1st International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2013), Workshop Track Proceedings / arXiv
References.SemanticInformation: Introduces the word2vec family of models (Skip-gram and CBOW) for learning continuous word embeddings efficiently from large corpora. The paper presents training algorithms and demonstrates that the learned vectors capture semantic and syntactic word relationships. The methods became foundational in NLP for representing word meaning in vector space.

References.PaperTitle: DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 20th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD '14)
References.SemanticInformation: Proposes DeepWalk, which learns node embeddings by treating truncated random walks on graphs as sentences and applying the Skip-gram model. This approach leverages local graph neighborhoods to produce representations useful for classification and link prediction. The method is scalable, unsupervised, and demonstrates strong performance on social network tasks.

References.PaperTitle: Understanding over-squashing and bottlenecks on graphs via curvature
References.Publication: The Tenth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2022), OpenReview.net
References.SemanticInformation: Analyzes the over-squashing problem in GNNs—where long-range information is compressed at bottlenecks—through notions of graph curvature. The authors provide theoretical and empirical insights linking curvature to information flow and over-squashing and propose diagnostics and potential remedies. Their work helps explain when and why information propagation fails in deep GNNs.

Discusses conceptual and practical challenges associated with interdisciplinary discourse, particularly in ecological and environmental contexts. The article highlights barriers such as differing terminologies, methods, and epistemologies across disciplines. It argues for awareness of these challenges when conducting and communicating interdisciplinary research.

References.PaperTitle: Representation learning on graphs with jumping knowledge networks
References.SemanticInformation: Introduces Jumping Knowledge (JK) networks, which allow flexible combination of node representations from different GNN layers to better capture both local and global information. JK networks improve performance on graphs with varying neighborhood sizes and help mitigate issues like oversmoothing. Experiments on benchmarks show that JK enhances representation quality and downstream task results.

References.PaperTitle: Two Sides of the Same Coin: Heterophily and Oversmoothing in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
References.Publication: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM)
References.SemanticInformation: Examines the relationship between heterophily (dissimilar neighbors) and oversmoothing in GCNs, showing how both phenomena affect model performance. The paper analyzes their interplay and provides empirical evidence across datasets. It offers insights into when traditional GCNs fail and suggests considerations for model design under heterophilic conditions.
